rv.q: Outrageously funny Mindelle plays Celine as an omniscient narrator who gloriously upstage everybody else.
Eventually 'Titanique' comes into its own as it revs up into increasing absurdity and the actors try to out-ham one another.
If you're not already a fan of the music and the movie, this mashup is unlikely to make you one.
The cast and creators' enthusiasm is infectious, and if you just let it wash over you, you'll have a boatload of fun.
I had a great time on my Titanic crossing and I think you will, too.
“Titanique” delivers. It’s really funny. And it doesn’t matter that the film “Titanic” is celebrating its 25th anniversary this month.

At its best, Titaníque explores the shadowy depths of Titanic's status as a cultural phenomenon that has left an indelible impression on the imaginations and sexual lives of millennials (the foggy car window receives a round of applause).
Titanique is a cheery diversion, and its fitting finale is the enthused audience singing along with Celine Dion.

cn.t: Critics find this campy Céline Dion-scored Titanic parody delivers sophomoric laughs and pure joy through its unabashedly cheesy premise, though some note it hits its marks better as scrappy Off-Broadway fare than high art.
